title: David Mourns Abner
reflectionText: Abner returned under a summons David had not sent, and violence met him inside Hebron’s gate. David answered publicly with mourning, fasting, lament, and a declaration that the killing was not his command. What is it to make grief and repudiation visible when another person’s wrongdoing touches one’s own house?
editorialNotes: Packet 017 initial writer output. Short-only owner plan. The retelling attributes Joab’s claims to Joab, keeps David unaware of Abner’s recall, and preserves David’s public repudiation, mourning, lament, weakness, and appeal for judgment within 2 Samuel 3:22-39.
